summary: Paul opposes community factions organized around named leaders.
The cross is contrasted with worldly wisdom and status.
Paul discusses divine wisdom and discernment through the Spirit.
Ministers are described as servants and the community as God's building.
Paul discusses stewardship, judgment, apostolic example and correction.
Paul calls for community discipline in a case of sexual misconduct and distinguishes judgment of insiders from outsiders.
Paul criticizes litigation between community members and lists conduct incompatible with God's kingdom.
Paul argues against sexual immorality using bodily union, belonging to Christ and the Spirit.
Marriage, mutual obligations and abstinence by agreement are discussed.
Paul differentiates an instruction attributed to the Lord from further guidance on mixed-belief marriages.
Paul discusses calling and social status, including circumcision, enslaved persons and the possibility of obtaining freedom, while urging believers to belong to Christ.
Paul offers counsel on marriage and singleness in view of present circumstances.
Knowledge about idol food is constrained by love and concern for conscience.
Paul discusses idols and identifies one God the Father and one Lord Jesus Christ in relation to creation.
Paul discusses apostolic rights and his decision not to exercise certain rights.
Paul describes adapting to different audiences and exercising self-discipline.
Israel's wilderness experiences are used as warnings against wrongdoing.
Idolatry, communal meals and concern for others shape food practices.
Paul addresses head coverings and relations between women and men, explicitly assuming women pray and prophesy in the passage.
Paul rebukes divisions and unequal eating at the communal supper.
Speech about Jesus is discussed in relation to the Spirit.
Paul describes diverse spiritual gifts and the interdependence of members of one body.
Paul places love above impressive gifts, describes its character and durability, and emphasizes its superiority to faith and hope in the current argument.
Prophecy and tongues are evaluated by their benefit to the assembled community.
Paul regulates orderly contributions and prophetic speech in the assembly; the contested instruction to women in verses 34–35 appears within this broader passage.
In the transmitted text, two verses demand silence of women in assemblies; some manuscript witnesses move them after verse 40 and scholars debate originality and scope.
textualNote: In several Western witnesses vv.34–35 occur after v.40, rather than following v.33. All presently known continuous manuscript witnesses preserve the verses somewhere; non-Pauline interpolation and quotation/refutation remain disputed hypotheses. Requires critical-apparatus review.

summary: Paul recounts received resurrection proclamation and his apostolic calling.
Paul argues that Christ's resurrection and the resurrection of the dead are inseparable, describing an ordered sequence of events.
Paul argues for resurrection using community practices and moral exhortation.
Paul discusses the transformed resurrection body and victory over death.
Paul instructs church members to set aside contributions according to their means and describes transparent delivery to Jerusalem.
Paul conveys greetings from Aquila and Prisca and the assembly in their house, without enumerating modern church offices.
Paul recalls conversion from idols and expectation of Jesus.
Paul describes missionary conduct, work and care for the community.
Paul discusses reception of the message and opposition in polemical language.
Paul recounts separation, Timothy's mission and prayer for the community.
Paul urges sexual holiness and avoidance of wrongdoing against others.
Paul commends mutual love, urges growth in care for others and gives practical counsel about quiet living, work and relationships with outsiders.
Paul comforts mourners with an account of the dead in Christ rising and believers meeting the Lord.
Paul describes the day of the Lord as unexpected and urges vigilance.
Paul asks the community to respect those who labor among them, support the weak, pursue good rather than revenge, pray continually and evaluate prophetic claims.
A letter of disputed Pauline authorship restricts women's teaching and exercise of authority over men, while referencing creation and childbirth; the scope and key Greek terms are debated.
The disputed Pauline letter outlines overseer and deacon qualifications; interpretation of gendered terms and the women of verse 11 is debated.
A later or disputed Pauline letter warns against love of money and instructs wealthy believers in generosity and good deeds.
Divine comfort amid suffering is connected to mutual support.
Paul urges forgiveness, comfort and reaffirmation of love after a punishment imposed by the majority.
Paul contrasts covenant ministries using letter, Spirit and veil imagery.
Ministry, bodily vulnerability and unseen hope are contrasted.
Paul discusses mortal existence, hope and accountability before Christ's judgment seat for deeds done in the body.
Paul describes reconciliation through Christ and the ministry of reconciliation.
Paul describes ministry hardships and appeals for mutual openness.
Paul urges separation from incompatible religious practices using temple imagery.
Paul discusses grief, repentance and renewed confidence in the community.
Paul appeals for generosity and equity in support of other believers.
Paul asks for a promised gift to be ready, connects giving with willing generosity, and describes relief for the saints.
Paul defends his authority and distinguishes his ministry from self-commendation.
Paul warns against rival apostles and competing proclamations.
Paul recounts hardships in a defense of his ministry.
Visions and weakness are discussed in relation to Christ's power.
Paul defends his conduct and expresses concern about community wrongdoing.
Paul warns of correction and urges self-examination and restoration.
Second Thessalonians links endurance under persecution with divine judgment and relief.
Second Thessalonians cautions against claims that the day of the Lord has arrived and describes preceding events.
Second Thessalonians addresses disorderly conduct and unwillingness to work, while retaining an admonition against treating offenders as enemies.
Second Timothy urges courage, fidelity to received teaching and willingness to suffer.
Second Timothy describes transmitting teaching, enduring hardship and remembering Jesus' resurrection.
Second Timothy urges avoidance of quarrels and gentle correction of opponents.
Second Timothy discusses persecution and the usefulness of scripture for teaching and training.
Second Timothy urges proclamation and perseverance while anticipating judgment and describing the speaker's approaching death.
Acts narrates believers sharing goods and proceeds from property sales so that needs within the community could be met.
Acts narrates the Jerusalem debate over circumcision for Gentiles and a communal decision with stated conditions.
Acts portrays Priscilla and Aquila explaining the way of God more accurately to Apollos; Acts is narrative context, not Paul's own account.
Colossians presents Christ as image of the invisible God and relates him to creation and reconciliation.
Colossians warns against deceptive teaching and judgment over food, festivals and ascetic regulations.
Colossians connects renewed life with changed conduct, compassion, forgiveness and love.
Colossians gives household instructions to wives, husbands, children, parents and enslaved persons.
Colossians instructs masters to act justly and urges prayer and wise conduct toward outsiders.
Ephesians describes salvation by grace through faith and good works as a purpose of renewed life.
Ephesians depicts reconciliation of Gentiles and Jews through Christ and a shared household of God.
Ephesians urges unity and describes diverse ministry roles contributing to communal maturity.
Ephesians urges truthful speech, restraint of anger, generosity and mutual forgiveness.
Ephesians frames marital obligations through submission and Christ's relationship to the assembly; interpretation of mutuality and hierarchy is disputed.
Ephesians addresses enslaved persons and masters, instructing masters against threats without explicitly abolishing slavery.
Paul defends his gospel and recounts his calling and early contacts.
Paul recounts recognition of his Gentile mission, notes Titus was not required to be circumcised, and reports the request to remember the poor (v. 10).
Paul describes a conflict over shared meals and argues that justification is not achieved by works of the Law.
Paul contrasts reception of the Spirit by faith with works of law.
Paul links reliance on works of the Law to a curse and relates the Abrahamic promise to faith and the Spirit.
Paul discusses the relationship between promise and law.
Paul describes the Law's supervisory role and a changed relationship to it through faith.
Paul identifies baptized believers as one in Christ across Jewish/Gentile, slave/free and male/female distinctions; effects on specific offices remain contested.
Inheritance, adoption and former religious observances are contrasted.
Paul appeals to the Galatians through their earlier relationship.
Paul uses Hagar and Sarah allegorically to contrast slavery and freedom.
Paul warns Gentile addressees against circumcision as a necessary covenant obligation and emphasizes faith expressed through love.
Paul says freedom should lead to serving others and summarizes the Law through neighbor-love.
Works of the flesh and fruit of the Spirit are contrasted.
Gentle restoration, burden bearing and doing good are urged.
Paul contrasts circumcision-based boasting with the cross and new creation.

title: The Word and the prologue
summary: The evangelist introduces the Word, creation, life and the Word becoming flesh; these are narrator claims, not speeches by Jesus.
textualNote: John 1:18 has significant Greek textual alternatives concerning how the Son is designated (often rendered 'only God' or 'only Son'); the prologue is the narrator's claim and requires apparatus-level review.

title: John the Baptist questioned
summary: Priests and Levites question John the Baptist about his identity and mission; his answers are not words of Jesus.

title: John the Baptist identifies Jesus
summary: John the Baptist testifies about Jesus and the Spirit; the narrator attributes these claims to John.

title: First disciples follow
summary: Jesus meets two followers of John, and Andrew brings Simon to him.

title: Philip and Nathanael
summary: Jesus calls Philip, speaks with Nathanael and promises a vision concerning the Son of Man.

title: Water turned to wine at Cana
summary: At a wedding, Jesus responds to his mother and a shortage of wine with the first sign in John's narrative.

title: Temple action and body-temple saying
summary: Jesus challenges commerce in the temple and speaks of raising the temple; the narrator interprets the reference as his body.

title: Signs and guarded trust
summary: The narrator reports public responses to signs and Jesus' reluctance to entrust himself to others.

title: Nicodemus and new birth
summary: Jesus speaks with Nicodemus about being born from above, the Spirit and the Son of Man.

title: God's love, light and judgment
summary: This theological passage develops themes of God's love and belief; the boundary between Jesus' speech and narrator comment is disputed.
textualNote: John 3:16–21 has no ancient quotation marks. Scholars differ whether this is Jesus speaking to Nicodemus or the evangelist's theological commentary. It is not included in the core sayings index as certain Jesus speech.

title: John the Baptist's final witness
summary: John the Baptist replies to concerns about Jesus' following and speaks of his own subordinate role.

title: Testimony about the one from above
summary: A theological testimony about the Son and divine authority has an uncertain speaker boundary, possibly John the Baptist or the narrator.
textualNote: The speaker of John 3:31–36 is uncertain: John the Baptist may continue from 3:27–30, or the evangelist may be commenting. Neither possibility makes it an unambiguous Jesus saying.

title: Travel and the well at Sychar
summary: Jesus travels through Samaria and rests at Jacob's well before the conversation begins.
Jesus converses with a Samaritan woman, whose later testimony brings people in her town to consider him; the text does not name a formal church office.
title: Jesus and the Samaritan woman
Return to Galilee
summary: Jesus continues to Galilee and is received after events witnessed in Jerusalem.

title: Healing an official's son
summary: Jesus responds to an official's plea for his child and speaks about belief before a healing.

title: Healing at the pool of Bethesda
summary: Jesus heals a man by a pool; John 5:3b–4 includes a disputed explanation about an angel stirring the water.
textualNote: John 5:3b–4, the explanation about an angel stirring the water, is absent from several early witnesses and considered a later expansion by many editors. This range remains numbered for edition compatibility, not as a verified original passage.

title: Opposition over Sabbath and the Father
summary: The narrator describes conflict about Sabbath healing and Jesus' relation to the Father.

title: The Son's life and judgment
summary: Jesus explains his dependence on the Father, the giving of life, resurrection and judgment.

title: Witnesses to the Son
summary: Jesus appeals to testimony, works, Scripture and Moses while challenging opponents' failure to believe.

title: Feeding a large crowd
summary: Jesus distributes bread and fish and withdraws after the crowd seeks to make him king.

title: Jesus approaches across the water
summary: The disciples encounter Jesus walking on the sea and hear his reassurance.

title: Work for lasting food
summary: Jesus redirects seekers from perishable bread toward trust in the one God has sent.

title: Bread from heaven
summary: Jesus speaks of bread from heaven and identifies himself as the bread of life.

title: The living bread
summary: Jesus responds to complaints about his origins and deepens the bread-from-heaven imagery.

title: Flesh, blood and life
summary: Jesus uses difficult language about his flesh, blood and life that has received varied sacramental and metaphorical interpretations.

title: Disciples dispute the hard teaching
summary: Followers call the teaching difficult, and some leave; Jesus speaks of Spirit and life.

title: The Twelve and a confession
summary: Jesus questions the Twelve, Peter confesses faith and the narrator comments about Judas.

title: Brothers and the festival journey
summary: Jesus discusses the festival with his brothers and travels privately amid divided opinion.

title: Teaching and judgment at the festival
summary: Jesus teaches publicly and contests claims about Sabbath observance and just judgment.

title: Debate about Jesus' origin
summary: People debate Jesus' origin and identity while he speaks in the temple.

title: Arrest attempt and departure language
summary: Authorities seek Jesus while he speaks of going where others cannot follow.

title: Living water during the festival
summary: Jesus calls the thirsty to come, and the narrator explains the reference to the Spirit.

title: Division over identity and origins
summary: Crowds and leaders dispute claims about Jesus; Nicodemus questions procedural fairness.

title: Disputed transition to the adulterous-woman story
summary: John 7:53 starts a story continuing at 8:1–11 that is absent from many early Greek witnesses and appears elsewhere in some later manuscripts.
textualNote: John 7:53 belongs to a continuous traditional episode through John 8:11. The passage is absent from the earliest major Greek witnesses and appears in differing manuscript locations. This is marked disputed rather than quoted as uncontested teaching.

title: Adulterous-woman episode — disputed placement
summary: A traditional account depicts Jesus responding to accusers and a woman charged with adultery; its place in the earliest text of John is highly disputed.
textualNote: The account of the woman accused of adultery (John 7:53–8:11) is absent from important early Greek manuscripts and appears elsewhere in some witnesses. It may be early tradition but its place in original John is strongly disputed; no saying from this unit is indexed as secure Johannine Jesus speech.

title: Light of the world and testimony
summary: Jesus declares himself the light of the world and disputes questions about his testimony.

title: Identity and the one who sent him
summary: Jesus warns opponents about failing to recognize his identity and speaks about being lifted up.

title: Truth, freedom and Abraham
summary: Jesus argues with interlocutors about freedom, descent from Abraham and listening to God.

title: Before Abraham and the identity claim
summary: Jesus disputes accusations and declares a relationship to Abraham that provokes an attempt to stone him.

title: Healing a man born blind
summary: Jesus heals a man born blind and rejects a simple blame assignment for his condition.

title: Inquiry into the healing
summary: Religious investigators question the healed man and his family; Jesus is largely absent from the dialogue.

title: Belief and spiritual blindness
summary: Jesus meets the man again and speaks of sight, judgment and blindness.
textualNote: John 9:35 differs among manuscripts between 'Son of Man' and 'Son of God'. The identity title should not be treated as textually unanimous.

title: The gate and the sheep
summary: Jesus uses images of a shepherd, a gate and sheep recognizing a voice.

title: The good shepherd
summary: Jesus contrasts his care for the sheep with hired hands and speaks of a wider flock.

title: The sheep, the Father and the Son
summary: Jesus speaks of his sheep hearing his voice and of his relationship with the Father.

title: Stones, Scripture and testimony
summary: Jesus responds to accusations about his identity through Scripture and his works, then withdraws.

title: Lazarus' illness and delayed journey
summary: Jesus hears of Lazarus' illness, waits before traveling and tells disciples about the coming event.

title: Martha and resurrection
summary: Jesus speaks with Martha about resurrection and life, and she confesses belief.

title: Mary's grief and Jesus' tears
summary: Mary meets Jesus amid grief, and the narrator describes his emotional response.

title: Lazarus raised
summary: Jesus prays and calls Lazarus from the tomb in a sign that draws witnesses.

title: Council plans Jesus' death
summary: Leaders react to the sign, and the narrator reports a plan to kill Jesus.

title: Anointing at Bethany
summary: Mary anoints Jesus at a meal, and Jesus responds to criticism about the cost of the perfume.

title: Entry into Jerusalem
summary: Crowds greet Jesus, and the narrator depicts authorities' reactions.

title: Grain of wheat and service
summary: Jesus uses a dying grain of wheat to speak of his death and the demands of following.

title: Troubled soul and the light
summary: Jesus addresses the coming hour, judgment, drawing people and walking while light remains.

title: Narrator explains unbelief
summary: The evangelist interprets public response using Isaiah and notes fears of social exclusion.

title: Public declaration about belief and judgment
summary: Jesus summarizes belief in the one who sent him and the relation of his words to judgment.

title: Footwashing as enacted example
summary: Jesus washes his followers' feet and directs them to follow the example of service.

title: Disclosure of betrayal
summary: Jesus alludes to Scripture and identifies a betrayer in a shared meal.

title: The new command and Peter's prediction
summary: Jesus commands mutual love and predicts Peter's denial.

title: The way, the Father and the works
summary: Jesus comforts followers, speaks of the Father's house and calls himself the way, truth and life.

title: Love, commandments and the Advocate
summary: Jesus links love for him with keeping his commands and promises another Advocate.

title: Peace and the Spirit's teaching
summary: Jesus speaks of the Spirit's teaching, leaves peace and announces an impending departure.

title: The vine and abiding in love
summary: Jesus uses the vine-and-branches image and commands followers to love one another.

title: Hostility from the world
summary: Jesus warns of opposition and promises that the Advocate and disciples will testify.

title: Exclusion and the Spirit of truth
summary: Jesus warns of persecution and describes the Advocate's work after his departure.

title: Sorrow transformed to joy
summary: Jesus answers confusion about his departure through a birth-pain comparison.

title: Prayer, directness and peace
summary: Jesus speaks about the Father, foretells desertion and calls followers to courage.

title: Jesus prays about glory
summary: Jesus addresses the Father about his work and glory before the world existed.

title: Jesus prays for the disciples
summary: Jesus prays for the followers entrusted to him and asks that they be kept in truth.

title: Jesus prays for future believers
summary: Jesus asks for unity among those who will believe through the disciples' witness.

title: Arrest in the garden
summary: An armed party arrests Jesus as he identifies himself and protects his followers.

title: Questions and Peter's denials
summary: Jesus faces questioning while Peter denies association with him; the narrated voices are distinct.

title: Pilate and the kingdom claim
summary: Jesus answers Pilate about kingship, truth and the origin of his kingdom.

title: Pilate's sentence and the claim of authority
summary: Jesus is mocked and sentenced while he responds to Pilate's assertion of power.

title: Crucifixion and care for his mother
summary: The narrative describes the crucifixion and Jesus' instruction involving his mother and a disciple.

title: Death and scriptural interpretation
summary: The narrator reports Jesus' death, the piercing of his side and scriptural interpretation.

title: Burial by Joseph and Nicodemus
summary: Joseph and Nicodemus bury Jesus according to local custom.

title: The empty tomb and two disciples
summary: Mary Magdalene reports the removed stone and two disciples investigate the tomb.
The risen Jesus addresses Mary Magdalene and commissions her to inform the disciples; a narrated commission does not itself settle all later institutional roles.
title: Mary Magdalene at the tomb
Peace, sending and forgiveness
summary: The risen Jesus appears to gathered disciples, sends them and speaks of forgiveness and retention of sins.
textualNote: John 20:23 requires contextual review when connecting the risen Jesus' words to later institutional authority; the passage's ecclesial application is disputed, even though the warning is interpretive rather than a settled manuscript variant.

title: Thomas and the risen Jesus
summary: Jesus appears again and answers Thomas' desire for evidence; the narrator records Thomas' response.

title: Narrator's stated purpose
summary: The evangelist explains that the account was selected to encourage belief, not to reproduce all signs.

title: Appearance and catch of fish
summary: The risen Jesus meets followers by the sea, directs a catch and shares a meal.

title: Peter and caring for sheep
summary: Jesus asks Peter repeatedly about love and charges him to care for the flock.

title: The beloved disciple and rumors
summary: Jesus speaks about another disciple, and the narrator corrects an inference about his death.

title: Final testimony and the books not written
summary: The Gospel closes with an editorial claim about witness and the many unrecorded acts of Jesus.
textualNote: John 21 is a canonical epilogue whose relationship to John 20:30–31 and the Gospel's compositional history is debated. The final narrator statements are not attributed to Jesus as speech.

title: Prologue to Theophilus
summary: The narrator describes researching and ordering inherited accounts for Theophilus; no saying of Jesus is recorded.

title: An announcement to Zechariah
summary: An angel announces John's birth while Zechariah serves at the temple; the speech belongs to the angel and Zechariah.

title: Annunciation to Mary
summary: An angel tells Mary of a forthcoming child and Mary replies; this is infancy narrative, not Jesus teaching.

title: Mary visits Elizabeth
summary: Elizabeth greets Mary and blesses her amid the account of their pregnancies.

title: Mary's praise song
summary: Mary's song announces God's attention to the lowly and reversal of the powerful; it is attributed to Mary, not Jesus.

title: John's birth and naming
summary: John is born and named; his father responds after a period of silence.

title: Zechariah's prophetic song
summary: Zechariah praises God's action on behalf of Israel and interprets John's future work; the words are his.

title: Jesus' birth in Bethlehem
summary: Luke narrates the journey to Bethlehem and Jesus' birth in a particular political setting.

title: Shepherds and angelic announcement
summary: Shepherds hear an angelic announcement, visit the infant and report what they heard.

title: Naming and temple rites
summary: Jesus is named and his family follows ritual obligations after his birth.

title: Simeon, Anna and recognition
summary: Simeon and Anna respond prophetically at the temple; neither is a saying of the infant Jesus.

title: Return to Nazareth
summary: Jesus' family returns home and the narrator describes his growth.

title: Twelve-year-old Jesus at the temple
summary: Jesus asks and answers questions at the temple and responds to his parents about his Father's concerns.

title: John's public ministry begins
summary: The narrative dates John's appearance and applies prophetic language to his ministry.

title: John's warnings and ethical instructions
summary: John calls for repentance, sharing and fair treatment and is imprisoned; the teaching is attributed to John.

title: Baptism and heavenly voice
summary: Jesus is baptized and a heavenly declaration follows; Luke does not report a sermon here.

title: Genealogy to Adam
summary: The narrator traces Jesus' ancestry through a genealogy ending with Adam.

title: Testing in the wilderness
summary: Jesus responds to the tempter through scriptural appeals in a narrative of temptation.

title: Return to Galilee
summary: Luke summarizes Jesus teaching in synagogues before giving the Nazareth scene.

title: Nazareth synagogue and rejection
summary: Jesus reads Isaiah and proclaims fulfillment; the hometown crowd resists his words.

title: An exorcism at Capernaum
summary: Jesus confronts a disruptive spirit, and witnesses respond to the authority of his words.

title: Healings at Simon's home
summary: Jesus heals Simon's mother-in-law and many sick or afflicted people.

title: The kingdom proclaimed elsewhere
summary: Jesus says that he must also announce God's kingdom to other towns.

title: A catch of fish and first disciples
summary: Jesus directs an unexpected catch and calls Simon toward a new mission.

title: Healing a man with skin disease
summary: Jesus heals a petitioner, sends him for priestly inspection and withdraws to pray.

title: Paralysis, forgiveness and authority
summary: Jesus challenges objections to his authority to forgive and heals a paralyzed man.

title: Levi, table fellowship and sinners
summary: Jesus calls Levi and answers objections to eating with people labeled sinners.

title: Fasting, garments and wine
summary: Jesus replies to questions about fasting with wedding, garment and wineskin images.

title: Grain on the Sabbath
summary: Jesus defends the disciples' grain-picking and discusses the Son of Man and the Sabbath.

title: Healing on the Sabbath
summary: Jesus challenges opponents to consider doing good and preserving life on the Sabbath.

title: Night prayer and choosing the Twelve
summary: Jesus prays and selects named apostles; this is primarily narrated commissioning.

title: Crowds seeking healing
summary: Luke describes a large gathered crowd and people healed before Jesus' sermon.
Luke juxtaposes blessings and woes involving poverty, hunger, wealth, and satisfaction.
title: Blessings and woes
Enemy-love and generosity
summary: Jesus calls hearers to love opponents, be merciful and give without assuming reciprocity.

title: Do not judge hypocritically
summary: Jesus warns against condemnation and uses the image of a speck and a log.

title: Trees recognized by their fruit
summary: Jesus compares the products of a person's heart to the fruit of a tree.

title: Hearing and acting: two builders
summary: Jesus illustrates obedience to his words through building on contrasting foundations.

title: A centurion asks for healing
summary: A centurion sends a request for his servant and Jesus comments on the man's trust.

title: Restoring a widow's son
summary: Jesus has compassion on a bereaved woman and restores her son to life.

title: John's messengers and Jesus' works
summary: Jesus answers messengers asking about his identity by pointing to healings and good news.

title: John and the contrasting generation
summary: Jesus interprets John's role and critiques inconsistent reactions to John and himself.

title: A woman, anointing and forgiven debt
summary: Jesus tells a debt illustration while defending a woman's actions and announcing forgiveness.
Luke names Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna and other women accompanying and materially supporting Jesus' mission; narrated participation is not a direct speech transcript.
title: Women accompanying Jesus
Sower and explanation
summary: Jesus gives a parable about scattered seed and explains different responses to God's word.

title: A lamp must be seen
summary: Jesus teaches about receiving and disclosing light and careful hearing.

title: Family redefined by hearing
summary: Jesus identifies family ties with hearing and acting on God's word.

title: Calming the storm
summary: Jesus calms the wind and waves, then questions the disciples about their faith.

title: A man restored among the Gerasenes
summary: Jesus releases a man from torment and tells him to report what God has done.

title: Jairus' daughter and a woman healed
summary: Jesus responds to a father and a woman seeking healing in intertwined episodes.

title: Sending the Twelve
summary: Jesus gives authority to the Twelve and directs travel, healing and proclamation.

title: Herod wonders about Jesus
summary: Herod considers rumors about Jesus' identity and seeks to see him.

title: Feeding the crowd
summary: Jesus welcomes a crowd, teaches about the kingdom and provides food through the disciples.

title: Peter's confession and suffering
summary: Jesus asks about his identity and predicts rejection, death and being raised.

title: Self-denial and following
summary: Jesus calls people to take up the cross and evaluates the cost of saving one's life.

title: Transfiguration on the mountain
summary: Jesus is transfigured before witnesses and a voice identifies him.

title: Healing a boy after the mountain
summary: Jesus heals a child amid the disciples' inability and the crowd's astonishment.

title: Another prediction of betrayal
summary: Jesus warns the disciples of his impending betrayal, which they do not grasp.

title: Greatness and welcoming a child
summary: Jesus responds to debate about status by placing a child before the disciples.

title: Someone working outside the circle
summary: Jesus responds to a report of another exorcist and discourages exclusionary control.

title: Turning toward Jerusalem
summary: Luke marks Jesus' determination to travel to Jerusalem and narrates a Samaritan village's rejection.

title: Would-be followers on the road
summary: Jesus answers three potential followers about the urgency and costs of following.

title: Sending the seventy or seventy-two
summary: Jesus commissions an enlarged group with instructions on travel, healing, hospitality and proclamation; the number is textually disputed.
textualNote: Manuscripts differ between seventy and seventy-two envoys in Luke 10:1,17; the precise number should not be asserted as unambiguous without a critical apparatus.

title: Warnings to rejecting towns
summary: Jesus pronounces woes and connects receiving messengers with receiving himself.

title: Return from the mission
summary: The envoys report success, and Jesus redirects their celebration toward belonging to God.
textualNote: Luke 10:17 also differs among manuscript witnesses over whether seventy or seventy-two envoys return; the reading remains disputed and requires critical-apparatus review.

title: Joy and revelation
summary: Jesus gives thanks and privately discusses the privilege of witnessing what disciples see.

title: Neighbor-love and the Samaritan
summary: A legal expert questions Jesus about life and the definition of a neighbor; Jesus tells the Samaritan story.
Luke presents Mary learning at Jesus' feet while Martha is occupied with hospitality; the passage should not be assumed to define a later church office.
title: Mary and Martha
Prayer and persistence
summary: Jesus gives prayer instruction, a prayer model and an analogy about asking.

title: Accusations of demonic power
summary: Jesus responds to critics by arguing that a divided kingdom cannot endure.

title: Empty house and hearing the word
summary: Jesus warns about a spirit's return and values hearing and keeping God's word.

title: Demand for a sign
summary: Jesus compares the audience to Nineveh and the queen of the south in a sign controversy.

title: The lamp and the eye
summary: Jesus speaks of light and the body's eye as a metaphor for inner perception.

title: Meals, woes and hypocrisy
summary: Jesus challenges ritual performance and the burdens placed on others by religious experts.

title: Beware hypocrisy; do not fear
summary: Jesus warns about hypocrisy, confession under pressure and reliance on divine help.
Jesus declines to arbitrate an inheritance and tells of a rich landowner whose hoarded abundance fails to secure his life.
title: The rich fool

summary: Jesus connects freedom from anxiety about necessities with seeking the kingdom and giving alms from possessions.
title: Anxiety, the kingdom and alms
Waiting servants and accountability
summary: Jesus describes attentive servants and warns leaders about abusing their authority.

title: Division and approaching crisis
summary: Jesus speaks of division and the conflict his mission can provoke.

title: Recognize the moment and settle disputes
summary: Jesus criticizes poor discernment of the times and urges settlement before judgment.

title: Repentance and the unfruitful fig tree
summary: Jesus rejects simplistic judgments about victims of disasters and tells a fruit-tree parable.

title: Healing a bent woman on the Sabbath
summary: Jesus heals a woman and answers objections by invoking liberation and Sabbath responsibility.

title: Mustard and leaven
summary: Jesus compares the kingdom to small beginnings that grow or transform a whole.

title: The narrow entrance
summary: Jesus answers a question about salvation and warns about a closed door and surprising reversals.

title: Lament for Jerusalem
summary: Jesus responds to a warning about Herod and laments Jerusalem's treatment of messengers.

title: Sabbath healing at a meal
summary: Jesus asks whether healing is permissible on the Sabbath and heals a man.

title: Choosing the lower place
summary: Jesus tells a meal-setting parable criticizing public status competition.

title: Invite those unable to repay
summary: Jesus urges a host to welcome the poor and disabled rather than only those who can reciprocate.

title: The great banquet
summary: Jesus describes an invitation refused by initial guests and extended to people otherwise excluded.

title: Counting the cost
summary: Jesus warns would-be followers to assess the demands of discipleship through vivid examples.

title: The lost sheep
summary: Jesus answers critics of his meals with sinners by portraying the joy of finding a lost sheep.

title: The lost coin
summary: Jesus compares recovery of a missing coin with joy over a person who repents.

title: A parent and two sons
summary: Jesus tells a story of a lost son welcomed home and an elder brother's resentment.

title: Shrewd manager and divided loyalties
summary: Jesus tells of a manager's response to loss of work and warns against serving both God and wealth.

title: The Pharisees and appearances
summary: Jesus challenges people who justify themselves publicly while God knows their hearts.
Luke places the proclamation of God's kingdom alongside a statement about the Law's endurance; the relation of the two requires interpretation.
title: The Law and God's kingdom
Divorce and remarriage
summary: Jesus speaks briefly about divorce and remarriage; its placement and relation to other Gospel versions require care.
A parable contrasts an affluent man's life with neglected Lazarus and depicts a reversal after death.
title: Rich man and Lazarus
Stumbling, repeated forgiveness and duty
summary: Jesus warns about causing others to stumble, instructs repeated forgiveness and uses a servant analogy.

title: Ten people with skin disease healed
summary: Jesus heals ten people, while a Samaritan returns to give thanks.

title: When the kingdom comes
summary: Jesus answers a question about the kingdom's coming and presence.

title: The days of the Son of Man
summary: Jesus warns about sudden judgment, false signs and the costs of clinging to life.

title: Persistent widow and an unjust judge
summary: Jesus uses a widow seeking justice to encourage persistence in prayer.

title: Pharisee and tax collector pray
summary: Jesus contrasts the self-congratulation of one worshiper with another's appeal for mercy.

title: Welcoming children
summary: Jesus urges that young children not be prevented from approaching.
Jesus challenges a ruler to distribute wealth to the poor and follow him, followed by warnings on wealth and entry to the kingdom.
title: The rich ruler
Suffering foretold
summary: Jesus predicts suffering, death and resurrection, but the disciples do not understand.

title: A blind man at Jericho
summary: Jesus responds to an appeal for mercy and restores sight as others praise God.
Luke describes Zacchaeus promising significant giving and restitution; Jesus announces salvation in this household.
title: Zacchaeus and restitution
Nobleman and entrusted money
summary: Jesus tells a parable about a nobleman, entrusted funds and later accountability near Jerusalem.

title: Entry into Jerusalem
summary: Luke narrates preparations for Jesus' arrival and the crowd's public praise.

title: Weeping over Jerusalem
summary: Jesus laments the city's inability to recognize the time of its visitation.

title: Temple teaching and disruption
summary: Jesus drives sellers from the temple and teaches there under hostile observation.

title: Authority challenged
summary: Jesus answers a question about his authority with a question about John's baptism.

title: The tenants of a vineyard
summary: Jesus tells a vineyard story interpreted as a challenge to entrusted leaders.

title: Caesar's taxes and God's claim
summary: Jesus answers a trap about tribute with a distinction between obligations.

title: A question about resurrection
summary: Jesus disputes a marriage-based challenge to belief in resurrection.

title: David's son and warnings about scribes
summary: Jesus poses a scriptural identity question and warns about exploited widows.

title: A widow's small offering
summary: Jesus notices a poor widow's offering; context includes critique of those exploiting widows.

title: Temple destruction and trouble
summary: Jesus foretells destruction and advises endurance under disturbances and persecution.

title: Jerusalem surrounded
summary: Jesus describes siege, flight and devastation in the language of impending judgment.

title: Signs and the Son of Man
summary: Jesus describes cosmic distress and calls followers to hope amid upheaval.

title: A fig tree and staying awake
summary: Jesus gives a seasonal illustration and urges vigilance rather than dullness.

title: Teaching by day and lodging outside
summary: The narrator summarizes Jesus' daily public teaching and nights spent outside the city.

title: Plot against Jesus and Judas' arrangement
summary: Leaders plan Jesus' death while Judas arranges betrayal.

title: Preparation for the Passover meal
summary: Jesus directs preparations and disciples secure a place for the meal.

title: Meal, covenant and betrayal
summary: Jesus speaks during a final meal and predicts betrayal; details of verses 19–20 vary among witnesses.
textualNote: The order and wording of the cup and bread, especially Luke 22:19b–20, differ among textual witnesses. Compare critical Greek editions before claiming a verbatim form.

title: Leadership, loyalty and future testing
summary: Jesus responds to a quarrel over status, discusses service and predicts denial.

title: Prayer at the Mount of Olives
summary: Jesus prays under distress; verses 43–44 mentioning an angel and sweat have important manuscript disagreement.
textualNote: Luke 22:43–44, describing angelic strengthening and sweat like blood, is absent from important early witnesses but present in others; authenticity is disputed, not settled by the displayed edition.

title: Betrayal and arrest
summary: Judas arrives with a group, and Jesus addresses betrayal and violence.

title: Peter's denial
summary: Peter denies association with Jesus and remembers the prediction.

title: Mockery and hearing before the council
summary: Jesus faces abuse and questioning about his identity.

title: Jesus before Pilate
summary: Jesus responds briefly to Pilate while accusers press charges.

title: Jesus before Herod
summary: Herod questions Jesus, who gives no answer, and the narrative describes mockery.

title: Sentencing and release of Barabbas
summary: Pilate seeks to avoid condemning Jesus, but the crowd demands crucifixion.

title: Words to mourning women
summary: Jesus tells women mourning him to consider impending suffering for Jerusalem.

title: Crucifixion and two criminals
summary: Luke reports Jesus' exchange with a condemned man; the prayer in verse 34 has manuscript variation.
textualNote: The prayer attributed to Jesus in Luke 23:34a is omitted in some early witnesses and retained by others. Scholarly opinions differ about whether this is an insertion or omission.

title: Death and witnesses
summary: Luke narrates Jesus' death and responses from witnesses.

title: Burial and women preparing spices
summary: Joseph buries Jesus and women observe the tomb and prepare burial spices.
Women report the empty tomb and angelic message to the apostles, whose initial reaction is disbelief; this is narrated witness rather than an ordination formula.
title: Women as witnesses at the tomb
Peter visits the tomb
summary: Peter sees evidence at the burial place; manuscript support for the verse has been discussed.
textualNote: The verse concerning Peter's visit to the tomb has textual-history discussion; this index records reference coverage only, not an adjudicated earliest wording.

title: The road to Emmaus
summary: Two disciples encounter the risen Jesus, who interprets Scripture and is recognized in the breaking of bread.

title: Appearance and commission in Jerusalem
summary: Luke narrates a further appearance, bodily demonstration and instruction to proclaim repentance and forgiveness.

title: Blessing, departure and worship
summary: Jesus blesses followers and departs; details of ascension wording have textual-history questions.
textualNote: The wording describing Jesus' departure or being carried into heaven in Luke 24:51 has a notable Western textual variant; exact wording requires a textual apparatus.

title: John and Jesus introduced
summary: John's proclamation, Jesus' baptism and testing introduce the narrative; John is the speaker in the proclamation.

title: Kingdom proclaimed
summary: Jesus announces the nearness of God's kingdom and calls for repentance and trust.

title: First followers called
summary: Jesus summons fishermen to follow him and gives their work a new purpose.

title: Synagogue teaching and exorcism
summary: The narrative reports teaching and an exorcism, but not the content of the synagogue lesson.

title: Healings in Capernaum
summary: Jesus heals Simon's mother-in-law and many others; no general instruction is recorded.

title: Prayer and itinerant mission
summary: Jesus prays and explains the purpose of continuing to preach in other towns.

title: Cleansing and priestly obligations
summary: Jesus responds to a man's request for cleansing and directs him to fulfill Moses' prescribed offering.

title: Forgiveness and a paralyzed man
summary: Jesus claims authority to forgive and heals a man carried by companions.

title: Levi and table fellowship
summary: Jesus eats with tax collectors and others labeled sinners, comparing his mission to a physician's work.

title: Fasting and wineskins
summary: Jesus answers a fasting question through wedding, fabric, and wineskin imagery.

title: Sabbath grain dispute
summary: Jesus appeals to David and describes Sabbath's purpose and the Son of Man's authority.

title: Sabbath healing
summary: Jesus frames a Sabbath question around doing good and preserving life.

title: Crowds and the Twelve
summary: Healings are reported and the Twelve are appointed for mission; most details are narrative.

title: Divided house and Spirit warning
summary: Jesus disputes claims of demonic agency and warns about blasphemy against the Holy Spirit.

title: Doing God's will defines kinship
summary: Jesus reorients the idea of family toward those who do God's will.

title: Sower and explanation
summary: Jesus tells and interprets a sowing parable about different responses to the word.

title: Lamp and measures
summary: Jesus speaks about hidden things, listening, and measure.

title: Growing seed
summary: Jesus compares the kingdom to seed growing through stages.

title: Mustard seed
summary: Jesus compares the kingdom to a tiny seed growing into a large plant.

title: Storm stilled
summary: Jesus calms the storm and asks the disciples why they fear and lack faith.

title: Gerasene man restored
summary: Jesus heals a man and sends him to tell others of mercy shown to him.

title: Woman healed and Jairus' daughter raised
summary: Two intertwined stories focus on healing, fear, trust, and restoration.

title: Rejection in Nazareth
summary: Jesus comments on the limited honor of a prophet among familiar people.

title: Sending of the Twelve
summary: Jesus gives travel and hospitality instructions to the Twelve.

title: Death of John the Baptist
summary: The narrator recounts John's execution; this is not a teaching by Jesus.

title: Feeding the crowd
summary: Jesus calls for rest, has compassion on the crowd, teaches and feeds it; his teaching's substance is not quoted.

title: Walking on the sea
summary: Jesus reassures the frightened disciples as the narrator notes their lack of understanding.

title: Healings at Gennesaret
summary: People seek healing by touching Jesus' clothing; no sustained discourse is recorded.

title: Tradition and Corban
summary: Jesus criticizes religious custom he says undermines the duty to honor parents.
Jesus disputes religious traditions concerning purity and defilement.
title: Purity and tradition — composite anchor
Defilement and the heart
summary: Jesus distinguishes external intake from conduct issuing from the heart; the treatment of verse 19 needs a textual note.

title: Syrophoenician mother's request
summary: A Gentile woman responds to Jesus' image about bread and children, and her daughter is healed.

title: Healing a deaf man
summary: Jesus heals a deaf man and enjoins discretion; the story is mainly action.

title: Feeding four thousand
summary: Jesus has compassion for a hungry crowd and feeds them.

title: Demand for a sign
summary: Jesus refuses to provide the requested sign in a dispute with Pharisees.

title: Warning against leaven
summary: Jesus cautions against the leaven of the Pharisees and Herod and challenges the disciples' understanding.

title: Sight restored in stages
summary: Jesus heals a blind man in stages.

title: Peter's confession and suffering
summary: Peter identifies Jesus as Christ and Jesus foretells rejection and death.

title: Take up the cross
summary: Jesus calls the crowd and disciples to self-denial and following him despite cost.

title: Kingdom promise and transfiguration
summary: Jesus speaks of the kingdom's power and later of Elijah; the transfiguration itself is narrated.

title: Child healed and belief
summary: Jesus addresses a father's plea and his disciples' inability to heal.

title: Prediction of death and rising
summary: Jesus predicts death and resurrection; disciples do not understand.

title: Greatness and a child
summary: Jesus associates greatness with becoming servant of all and welcoming a child.

title: Outsider acting in Jesus' name
summary: Jesus cautions disciples against stopping someone acting in his name.

title: Warnings about stumbling
summary: Jesus first warns against causing a vulnerable believer to stumble (v. 42), then uses severe body-part imagery about what causes one's own stumbling (vv. 43–48), concluding with salt and peace (vv. 49–50). Verse inclusion varies in textual traditions.
Jesus responds to questions about divorce by appealing to creation and covenant.
title: Marriage and divorce
Welcome children
summary: Jesus welcomes children and connects their example to receiving God's kingdom.
Jesus challenges a wealthy man and discusses the difficulty of entering God's kingdom with riches.
title: Rich man and possessions
Prediction on the road
summary: Jesus foretells mockery, execution and resurrection in Jerusalem.

title: Servant leadership
summary: Jesus rejects dominative leadership among disciples and frames his mission as service.

title: Bartimaeus healed
summary: Jesus responds to a blind beggar's plea and attributes healing to faith.

title: Entry into Jerusalem
summary: Jesus arranges his entry and enters Jerusalem to public acclaim; this is mainly narrative.

title: Fig tree and temple action
summary: Jesus pronounces against a fig tree and disrupts commerce in the temple, citing prayer for all nations.

title: Faith, prayer and forgiveness
summary: Jesus draws a lesson about faith, prayer and forgiving others; verse 26 is textually disputed.

title: Challenge over authority
summary: Jesus counters an authority question with a question about John's baptism.

title: Wicked tenants
summary: Jesus portrays tenants abusing servants and killing the owner's son; opponents understand the parable as directed at them.

title: Taxes and Caesar
summary: Jesus answers a taxation challenge by distinguishing what is Caesar's from what belongs to God.

title: Resurrection debate
summary: Jesus disputes a denial of resurrection using scripture and an account of resurrected life.

title: Greatest commandments
summary: Jesus centers love of God and neighbor as foundational commandments.

title: David and the Messiah
summary: Jesus questions a conventional reading of the Messiah as David's son.

title: Warning against scribal exploitation
summary: Jesus criticizes ostentatious status and devouring widows' houses.

title: Widow's offering
summary: Jesus comments on a poor widow's contribution; whether the passage praises her or critiques the setting is disputed.

title: Temple destruction and early warnings
summary: Jesus predicts the temple's destruction and warns against deception and alarm.

title: Persecution and witness
summary: Jesus anticipates persecution and instructs disciples to persevere in testimony.

title: Distress and false claimants
summary: Jesus speaks of flight from danger and warns against deceptive messianic claims.

title: Son of Man and gathering
summary: Jesus depicts cosmic upheaval and the Son of Man gathering chosen ones.

title: Fig tree and vigilance
summary: Jesus uses a fig tree comparison and cautions that the timing is unknown.

title: Plot, anointing and betrayal
summary: Jesus defends a woman's costly act in the setting of a plot and Judas' betrayal; other scenes are narrated.

title: Passover arrangements and betrayer
summary: Jesus directs meal preparations and predicts betrayal.

title: Bread and covenant cup
summary: Jesus interprets shared bread and wine in relation to his body, blood, covenant and kingdom.

title: Denial predicted
summary: Jesus predicts desertion and Peter's repeated denial.

title: Gethsemane and watchfulness
summary: Jesus prays in distress and calls his disciples to watch and pray.

title: Arrest and council
summary: Jesus is arrested, questioned by the high priest, and responds about identity and vindication.

title: Peter's denials
summary: Peter denies knowing Jesus, matching an earlier prediction; Jesus is not speaking here.

title: Jesus before Pilate
summary: Jesus answers Pilate briefly and is otherwise largely silent.

title: Sentence and crucifixion
summary: The narrative recounts Barabbas, mockery and crucifixion; Jesus does not give a new teaching discourse.

title: Jesus' death
summary: Jesus voices a lament connected to Psalm 22 and dies; this is not a general ethical instruction.

title: Women witnesses and burial
summary: Women observe events and Jesus is buried; narrative testimony rather than recorded teaching.

title: Empty tomb and messenger
summary: Women hear the young man's announcement at the empty tomb; Jesus does not speak in this passage.

title: Longer ending of Mark
summary: A textually disputed ending includes attributed words of the risen Jesus concerning mission and signs; do not present as uncontested Markan teaching.
textualNote: Mark 16:9–20 is absent from some early witnesses and commonly considered a later ending; scholarly and confessional assessments differ.

title: Genealogy of Jesus
summary: Matthew begins by tracing a genealogy that links Jesus with Abraham and David; it is narrated ancestry, not speech by Jesus.

title: Birth and naming
summary: Joseph receives guidance in a dream about Mary's pregnancy and names the child Jesus; no direct speech by Jesus is reported.

title: Magi and Herod
summary: Visitors seek the newborn king, Herod reacts, and the visitors return by another route; this is infancy narrative.

title: Flight and return
summary: Dream-guided movements take the family to Egypt and later Nazareth amid danger under rulers; this is narrative context.

title: John the Baptist preaches
summary: John announces repentance and judgment and baptizes; his exhortations should not be labeled speeches of Jesus.

title: Baptism of Jesus
summary: Jesus comes to John for baptism and the scene presents a heavenly declaration; it is an identity narrative.

title: Testing in the wilderness
summary: Jesus answers the tempter with scriptural appeals; the dialogue should be read with its narrative framing.

title: Beginning of kingdom proclamation
summary: Matthew depicts Jesus relocating to Galilee and proclaiming repentance because heaven's kingdom has drawn near.

title: Calling the first followers
summary: Jesus summons fishermen to follow, and the narrative describes their response.

title: Teaching and healings throughout Galilee
summary: Matthew summarizes teaching, proclamation and cures without transcribing individual sermon units.

title: Blessings at the mountain
summary: Jesus pronounces blessings on persons with particular conditions and practices; Matthew's wording differs from Luke's blessings and woes.

title: Salt and light
summary: Jesus instructs disciples to be salt and light, drawing on images of public visibility and good deeds.
Jesus speaks of fulfilling the Law and the continuing importance of its commands.
title: Law and fulfillment

summary: In a series of examples, Matthew's Jesus intensifies and reframes obligations around murder, adultery, oath-taking, retaliation and love of enemies.
title: Ethics in the mountain discourse
Giving without display
summary: Jesus instructs about almsgiving without staging it for public approval.

title: Prayer and forgiveness
summary: Jesus contrasts performative prayer with directed prayer, including the prayer model and reciprocal forgiveness.

title: Fasting without display
summary: Jesus directs disciples not to make fasting into a public display of piety.
Jesus contrasts earthly and heavenly treasure and presents serving God and wealth as competing masters.
title: Treasure and competing masters

summary: Jesus instructs hearers not to be consumed with anxiety about food and clothing, directing them toward God's kingdom.
title: Anxiety and seeking the kingdom
Judging and self-scrutiny
summary: Jesus warns against hypocritical condemnation and uses an illustration about a speck and a plank.

title: Asking and treating others well
summary: Jesus urges persistent asking, portrays divine generosity and states a reciprocal rule for treating others.

title: Entrances, fruit and false profession
summary: Jesus warns about narrow entry, misleading teachers, actions and professions that lack obedience.

title: Two builders
summary: Jesus compares people who hear and act on his teaching with builders choosing differing foundations.

title: Crowds react to the sermon
summary: The crowd responds to the authority of Jesus' teaching, and Matthew closes the discourse in narration.

title: Cleansing a man with skin disease
summary: Jesus heals a petitioner and instructs him to show himself to a priest and make the prescribed offering.

title: The centurion's request
summary: Jesus responds to a military officer's request for healing and comments on unexpected faith.

title: Healings in Peter's household
summary: Matthew reports a sequence of healings and links it to a scriptural fulfillment motif.

title: Costs of following
summary: Jesus answers would-be followers with sayings about insecurity and competing obligations.

title: Storm and fear
summary: Jesus and disciples are in a storm, and Jesus challenges their fear before calming it.

title: Two demoniacs across the lake
summary: Matthew narrates an encounter with two afflicted people and the reaction of a nearby town.

title: Paralysis and authority to forgive
summary: Jesus addresses a paralyzed man and responds to objections about forgiveness, then heals him.

title: Calling Matthew and eating with outsiders
summary: Jesus calls a tax collector and defends his company through a physician analogy and a call to mercy.

title: Fasting and new wine
summary: Jesus responds to questions about fasting with images of a wedding, cloth and wineskins.

title: Leader's daughter and bleeding woman
summary: Matthew narrates intertwined healing encounters with a dying child and a woman seeking help.

title: Sight and speech restored
summary: Two blind people and a man unable to speak are helped, with differing reactions from observers.

title: Compassion and need for laborers
summary: The narrative summarizes widespread teaching and healing and records Jesus' instruction to pray for laborers.

title: The twelve commissioned
summary: Matthew names the Twelve and presents their appointment; these verses are narrative framing.

title: Instructions for a mission journey
summary: Jesus directs an initial mission, including destination, healing, provision, hospitality and responses to rejection.

title: Danger and persecution in mission
summary: Jesus warns followers of opposition, trial and family tensions during mission.

title: Fear, witness and confession
summary: Jesus encourages faithful public witness and warns against denying allegiance to him.

title: Division, loyalty and hospitality
summary: Jesus speaks of competing loyalties, the cost of following and how receiving emissaries matters.

title: John's messengers question Jesus
summary: Jesus answers messengers of John by pointing to healing, proclamation and the blessedness of not stumbling.

title: John, messengers and this generation
summary: Jesus interprets John's role and criticizes the generation's inconsistent reactions to John and himself.

title: Woes to unresponsive towns
summary: Jesus warns towns where many deeds occurred without repentance.

title: Thanksgiving and invitation to rest
summary: Jesus thanks the Father and invites burdened people to take up his yoke and learn from him.

title: Sabbath controversies
summary: Jesus argues about permitted conduct and healing on the Sabbath, provoking hostile responses.

title: Healing and servant motif
summary: Jesus withdraws, heals, and Matthew applies a prophetic servant passage; most of this unit is narration.

title: Accusations, words and divided powers
summary: Jesus rebuts claims that his work comes from demonic power and connects speech with a person's interior life.

title: Signs and a judgment warning
summary: Jesus responds to a demand for a sign with the Jonah comparison and warnings about an unresponsive generation.

title: The family of those who obey
summary: Jesus reframes family around doing the will of his heavenly Father.

title: The sower and varied ground
summary: Jesus tells a sowing parable depicting markedly different outcomes for scattered seed.

title: Why parables and how to hear the sower
summary: Jesus answers a question about parables and explains several differing responses to a message.

title: Wheat and weeds growing together
summary: Jesus describes rival sowings and a deferred separation at harvest.

title: Mustard and leaven
summary: Jesus gives short growth images and the narrator describes the use of parables.

title: Weeds explained
summary: Jesus privately interprets the field, harvest and agents in the earlier parable.

title: Treasure, pearl, net and learned scribe
summary: Jesus gives a series of images about value, discernment and the kingdom's outcome.

title: Resistance in the hometown
summary: Matthew narrates doubts among people familiar with Jesus' family and concludes the parables setting.

title: Herod and John's death
summary: The narrative recounts John the Baptist's execution and court intrigue without attributing the episode's speech to Jesus.

title: Feeding a crowd
summary: Jesus has compassion on a gathering, heals and distributes food through the disciples.

title: Walking on water and fear
summary: The disciples confront the wind and Jesus approaches; Matthew includes Peter's attempt to walk toward him.

title: Healings in Gennesaret
summary: People bring the ill for healing and seek to touch Jesus' garment.
Jesus challenges traditions that circumvent obligations toward parents and argues that morally defiling actions arise from the heart.
title: Tradition and what defiles
A Canaanite woman's request
summary: A Gentile woman asks for her daughter's healing, and the exchange presses a question of priority and faith.

title: Many people healed
summary: Matthew summarizes healing of people with differing disabilities and their praise of Israel's God.

title: Feeding the four thousand
summary: Jesus takes account of the crowd's hunger and provides a second large-scale feeding.

title: Demand for a sign and warning about leaven
summary: Jesus disputes a request for signs and cautions his disciples about misleading teaching.

title: Peter's confession and keys
summary: Jesus asks about his identity and answers Peter with language about rock, community and binding and loosing.

title: Prediction of suffering and the cost of following
summary: Jesus announces suffering and calls disciples to deny themselves and take up the cross.

title: Transfiguration and the Elijah question
summary: Jesus is transfigured before selected followers and later responds to an Elijah question.

title: Healing and the disciples' failed attempt
summary: Jesus heals a boy and addresses the disciples' inability; verse 21 is textually disputed in some editions.
textualNote: The WEBP source footnote identifies Matthew 17:21 as absent from the NU text. This literary range remains indexed for navigation, but the prayer-and-fasting clause requires separate critical-edition review.

title: A second prediction of suffering
summary: Jesus tells the disciples of betrayal, death and being raised.

title: Temple tax and sons
summary: Jesus discusses a tax question with Peter and directs an unusual means of paying it.

title: Greatness, children and causing stumbling
summary: Jesus answers a status question by placing a child in view and warning about harming vulnerable believers.

title: The lost sheep
summary: Jesus draws on a shepherd's search to teach about not despising the vulnerable.

title: Repairing relationships in a community
summary: Jesus gives steps for addressing wrongdoing and describes agreement and gathering among disciples.

title: Unforgiving servant
summary: Jesus responds to Peter's question on forgiveness with a story of debt and mercy withheld.

title: Marriage, divorce and continence
summary: Jesus debates marriage and divorce, responding to religious opponents and disciples.

title: Children brought for blessing
summary: Jesus receives children brought by adults, opposing attempts to block them.
Matthew narrates Jesus challenging a wealthy questioner to sell possessions, give to the poor and follow, and his subsequent warning about wealth.
title: Rich seeker and following Jesus
Laborers in a vineyard
summary: Jesus depicts workers paid on surprising terms to challenge ideas of desert and rank.

title: Suffering foretold near Jerusalem
summary: Jesus predicts betrayal, condemnation and being raised after death.

title: Status, serving and greatness
summary: Jesus answers a request for places of honor by contrasting ruling over others with serving them.

title: Two blind men near Jericho
summary: Jesus responds to pleas for mercy and restores sight; Matthew narrates two recipients.

title: Entry into Jerusalem
summary: Matthew narrates a public arrival with symbolic actions and responses from the crowd.

title: The temple disrupted
summary: Jesus overturns merchants' tables in the temple and disputes how the space is being used.

title: Fig tree and trust
summary: A fig-tree episode leads to teaching about faith and prayer.

title: Authority questioned
summary: Temple leaders question Jesus' authority, and he responds with a question about John's baptism.

title: Two sons
summary: Jesus tells a story about words and action as part of a dispute over response to John.

title: Tenants and the vineyard
summary: Jesus tells a vineyard story provoking reactions from leaders who recognize its critical force.

title: Wedding banquet and invited guests
summary: Jesus tells of rejected invitations, new guests and a guest judged unprepared.

title: Tax and obligation to Caesar
summary: Jesus answers a trap about tax by contrasting imperial and divine claims.

title: Debate about resurrection
summary: Jesus answers a hypothetical marriage question and argues about resurrection and divine life.

title: The greatest commandments
summary: Jesus identifies love of God and neighbor as central to Law and Prophets.

title: David's son and identity
summary: Jesus poses a scriptural question about the Messiah and David's description of him.

title: Status, teaching and humility
summary: Jesus challenges status-seeking among religious teachers and instructs disciples about leadership.

title: Woes against hypocrisy and exploitation
summary: Jesus criticizes practices of religious leaders, using a series of woes and scriptural allusions.

title: Lament over Jerusalem
summary: Jesus laments resistance to his summons and describes judgment and future recognition.

title: Temple destruction and early disturbances
summary: Jesus foretells the temple's fall and describes conflict, persecution and a worldwide proclamation.

title: Distress and the coming of the Son of Man
summary: Jesus describes severe distress, deceptive claims and the gathering of the chosen; chronology and imagery require care.

title: Fig tree and vigilance
summary: Jesus uses a fig tree and an unexpected arrival to call for watchfulness.

title: Faithful and abusive servants
summary: Jesus contrasts caretakers acting responsibly with those exploiting their position during an absence.

title: Ten bridesmaids
summary: Jesus illustrates readiness through a wedding procession and differing preparations.

title: Entrusted resources and accountability
summary: Jesus tells of servants entrusted resources and later called to account, with difficult judgment imagery.
The Son of Man's judgment scene centers on treatment of the hungry, stranger, sick, and imprisoned.
title: Judgment and treatment of others
Plot, anointing and betrayal arrangement
summary: Matthew narrates schemes against Jesus, a costly anointing, and Judas' agreement to betray him.

title: Passover meal and covenant words
summary: Jesus shares a meal with disciples, predicts betrayal, and associates bread and cup with his approaching death.

title: Prediction of falling away and Peter's denial
summary: Jesus warns of his followers' failure, while Peter promises loyalty.

title: Prayer in Gethsemane
summary: Jesus prays about the coming ordeal and urges followers to watch and pray.

title: Arrest of Jesus
summary: Judas approaches with an armed crowd; Jesus addresses violence and the event's relation to Scripture.

title: The hearing before the council
summary: Jesus faces questioning, accusation and mistreatment before religious leaders.

title: Peter's denials
summary: Peter denies knowing Jesus in the courtyard, fulfilling the earlier prediction.

title: Judas and the handed-over Jesus
summary: Judas returns the payment and the chief priests arrange the field purchase as Jesus is transferred to Pilate.

title: Pilate, the crowd and a verdict
summary: Jesus is questioned and the crowd demands a different prisoner as Pilate orders crucifixion.

title: Mockery and crucifixion
summary: Soldiers and bystanders mock the crucified Jesus; their words are not his teachings.

title: Death and accompanying signs
summary: Matthew narrates Jesus' death, the temple veil and reactions of watchers.

title: Burial and guarded tomb
summary: Joseph of Arimathea buries Jesus, women remain nearby, and guards are assigned.
Women receive an announcement at the tomb and meet the risen Jesus, who tells them to convey a message to the brothers.
title: Women at the tomb
Guards and the alternative report
summary: Matthew describes guards reporting events and a counter-story about the disappearance of the body.

title: Commission to teach the nations
summary: Matthew describes the risen Jesus addressing disciples with a commission to make disciples and teach obedience.
Paul greets Philemon and others and gives thanks for faith and love.
Paul appeals rather than simply commands Philemon to receive Onesimus as a beloved brother, while the letter leaves questions of legal manumission and slavery unresolved.
Paul requests lodging and sends greetings and a closing blessing.
Paul discusses partnership, imprisonment and the advance of the gospel.
The community is urged to stand together amid opposition.
Paul urges unity and humility through concern for others, presenting Christ's self-emptying and exaltation as a model; interpretation of the Christ hymn's source and form is debated.
Obedience, divine activity and conduct without grumbling are urged.
Timothy and Epaphroditus are commended for their service.
Paul contrasts inherited credentials with righteousness associated with Christ.
Paul describes pursuit of the goal and heavenly citizenship.
Paul urges reconciliation between Euodia and Syntyche, whom he describes as having struggled alongside him in the gospel.
Paul encourages joy, gentle conduct, prayer with thanksgiving and freedom from anxiety while speaking about God's peace.
Paul discusses contentment and the community's material support.
The gospel is presented as God's saving power for Jew and Greek, with righteousness associated with faith.
Paul describes human wrongdoing, idolatry and divine judgment.
Paul describes impartial divine judgment according to deeds, including the role of the Law and conscience.
Paul connects divine righteousness, faith, grace, redemption and Christ's blood.
Paul contrasts justification by faith with works of the Law while insisting that faith does not nullify the Law.
Abraham's righteousness is discussed in relation to faith and circumcision.
The promise to Abraham is associated with faith rather than law.
Justification, reconciliation, hope and endurance in suffering are connected.
Adam and Christ are contrasted in relation to sin, death and grace.
Baptism into Christ's death is connected to a renewed way of life.
Freedom from sin is expressed through slavery imagery and obedience to righteousness.
Paul uses an analogy about law to discuss a new relationship to service in the Spirit.
Paul rejects the equation of Law with sin and describes the commandment as holy, just and good.
Paul presents what the Law could not accomplish through weakened human flesh and speaks of its righteous requirement being fulfilled.
Life in the Spirit is contrasted with life according to the flesh.
Paul connects suffering with future glory, hope and confidence in divine love.
Paul discusses Israel, divine election and mercy.
Israel and Gentiles are discussed in relation to righteousness and faith.
Paul describes Christ as the telos of the Law; whether this means endpoint, goal, culmination or a combination is debated.
Paul connects faith, confession, proclamation and hearing.
Israel's remnant and Gentile inclusion are discussed using olive tree imagery.
Paul discusses Israel's future, mercy and divine wisdom.
Renewed discernment, humility and diverse community gifts are urged.
Paul exhorts believers to sincere love, share in the needs of fellow believers, and practice hospitality.
Paul exhorts the Roman believers to bless persecutors, refuse retaliation, seek peace where possible and answer harm with good.
Paul urges subordination to governing authorities, describes rulers' claimed public functions, and speaks about taxes, respect and accountability.
Paul connects love of neighbor with the fulfillment of the Law and specifies several commandments.
Disagreements over food and days are addressed through mutual acceptance.
Conscience and avoiding harm to others constrain personal freedom.
The strong are urged to support the weak and welcome one another.
Paul describes bringing contributions from Gentile churches for the poor among the believers in Jerusalem.
Paul commends Phoebe as a diakonos linked to the Cenchreae assembly and a prostatis to many; the scope of these terms is debated.
Paul publicly recognizes Phoebe, Prisca, Junia and other women as servants, coworkers, laborers or notable persons within early Christian networks; individual role terms are disputed.
Paul greets Prisca, Aquila, Mary, and Junia alongside others; Junia's relation to the apostles and the significance of the role terms are debated.
A letter of disputed Pauline authorship instructs older women to teach what is good to younger women within a domestic-ethical framework.
